# Command line

<!-- Generated by `chipload reference`; do not edit. Regenerate with CHIPLOAD_UPDATE_GOLDEN=1 cargo test -p chipload-cli --test guide. -->

Every command takes `--json`: one JSON object instead of text (see [Scripting](../scripting.md)). `chipload --help` and `chipload COMMAND --help` print the same help in the terminal.

## `chipload inspect`

Dump units, entities, contours and issues of a DXF or a project

```text
chipload inspect <FILE> [OPTIONS]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<FILE>` | A .dxf drawing or a .chipload project. |
| `--units <UNITS>` | Units of a DXF that does not declare them. One of: `mm`, `inch`. |

## `chipload new`

Create an empty project, to draw in or import a DXF into later (`update --from`)

```text
chipload new [OPTIONS]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `-o, --output <OUTPUT>` | The project to write (.chipload) Required. |
| `--machine <MACHINE>` | The machine profile to start from (default: your default machine) |

## `chipload import`

Create a project from a DXF

```text
chipload import <DXF> [OPTIONS]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<DXF>` | The DXF. |
| `--units <UNITS>` | Units of a DXF that does not declare them. One of: `mm`, `inch`. |
| `-o, --output <OUTPUT>` | The project to write (.chipload) Required. |
| `--machine <MACHINE>` | The machine profile to start from (default: your default machine) |

## `chipload update`

Replace a project's imported drawing with a new version of the DXF

```text
chipload update <PROJECT> [OPTIONS]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<PROJECT>` | The project (.chipload) |
| `--from <FROM>` | The new DXF. Required. |
| `--units <UNITS>` | Units of the new DXF, if they differ from the last import. One of: `mm`, `inch`. |
| `-o, --output <OUTPUT>` | Where to write the result; default: the project itself. |

## `chipload plan`

Plan a project's toolpath without writing G-code

```text
chipload plan <PROJECT> [OPTIONS]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<PROJECT>` | The project (.chipload) |
| `--set <PATH=VALUE>` | For this run only: set a project value by path, e.g. `stock.thickness=18` (see `chipload set`). The project file isn't changed. Repeatable. |

## `chipload run`

Generate checked G-code from a project

```text
chipload run <PROJECT> [OPTIONS]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<PROJECT>` | The project (.chipload) |
| `-o, --output <OUTPUT>` | Where to write the G-code. With several tools and one file per tool: part.nc gives part-1-T1.nc, part-2-T2.nc, ... Required. |
| `--tool-change <TOOL_CHANGE>` | For this run only: one file per tool, or one file with M6 tool changes (default: the project's machine setting) One of: `files` (One G-code file per tool group), `program` (One file with `T<n> M6` at each tool change). |
| `--no-sheet` | Don't write the setup sheet (by default `part-sheet.html` next to `part.nc`) |
| `--set <PATH=VALUE>` | For this run only: set a project value by path, e.g. `stock.thickness=18` (see `chipload set`). The project file isn't changed. Repeatable. |

## `chipload simulate`

Simulate the material a project's program removes (docs/specs/simulation.md): print the numbers and write a shaded top view (PNG). The job is generated and checked as by `run`; no G-code is written

```text
chipload simulate <PROJECT> [OPTIONS]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<PROJECT>` | The project (.chipload) |
| `-o, --output <OUTPUT>` | Where to write the image (.png); default: the project's name with `-sim.png`. |
| `--cell <CELL>` | Cell size, mm (default: automatic, from the stock's size) |
| `--no-image` | Print the numbers only. |
| `--after <N>` | The stock after only the first N moves of the program (docs/specs/playback.md §5), for tests and scripts. |
| `--set <PATH=VALUE>` | For this run only: set a project value by path, e.g. `stock.thickness=18` (see `chipload set`). The project file isn't changed. Repeatable. |

## `chipload sheet`

Write a project's setup sheet for the operator (HTML), without the G-code. The job is generated and checked as by `run`

```text
chipload sheet <PROJECT> [OPTIONS]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<PROJECT>` | The project (.chipload) |
| `-o, --output <OUTPUT>` | Where to write the sheet (.html) Required. |
| `--gcode <GCODE>` | The G-code the sheet is for, as given to `run -o`, for its file names (default: the project's name with the post's extension) |
| `--tool-change <TOOL_CHANGE>` | For this sheet only: one file per tool, or one file with M6 tool changes. One of: `files` (One G-code file per tool group), `program` (One file with `T<n> M6` at each tool change). |
| `--set <PATH=VALUE>` | For this run only: set a project value by path, e.g. `stock.thickness=18` (see `chipload set`). The project file isn't changed. Repeatable. |

## `chipload render`

Render a toolpath JSON (as `plan --json` prints under "program") through a post-processor. For testing posts; the output is NOT checked, use `run` to cut

```text
chipload render <PROGRAM> [OPTIONS]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<PROGRAM>` | Toolpath JSON file. |
| `--post <POST>` | Built-in post-processor. Default: `grbl`. |

## `chipload check`

Check a G-code program against a project's stock, safe height and machine limits

```text
chipload check <GCODE> [OPTIONS]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<GCODE>` | G-code file to check. |
| `--job <JOB>` | The project (or job) the program was generated from. Required. |
| `--tool <TOOL>` | The project's tool that cuts this program, for its stock margin (one file of a set written one file per tool). Default: the largest tool the project uses. |

## `chipload op`

Change an operation of a project

### `chipload op tool`

Set the tool an operation cuts with (docs/specs/tool-per-operation.md §7). The tool must be in the project: copy one in from your library with `tool use`

```text
chipload op tool <PROJECT> [OPTIONS]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<PROJECT>` | The project (.chipload) |
| `--op <OP>` | The operation, 1-based as listed. Required. |
| `--tool <TOOL>` | The tool's id in the project. Required. |
| `-o, --output <OUTPUT>` | Where to write the result; default: the project itself. |

### `chipload op add-rest`

Add a rest pocket after a pocket (docs/specs/rest-machining.md §10): its shapes and depths, cut with a smaller tool, clearing only what the pocket's tool leaves

```text
chipload op add-rest <PROJECT> [OPTIONS]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<PROJECT>` | The project (.chipload) |
| `--op <OP>` | The pocket, 1-based as listed. Required. |
| `--tool <TOOL>` | The smaller tool's id in the project. Required. |
| `-o, --output <OUTPUT>` | Where to write the result; default: the project itself. |

### `chipload op rest`

Make a pocket clear only what a larger tool leaves (docs/specs/rest-machining.md)

```text
chipload op rest <PROJECT> [OPTIONS]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<PROJECT>` | The project (.chipload) |
| `--op <OP>` | The pocket, 1-based as listed. Required. |
| `--after-tool <AFTER_TOOL>` | The larger tool's id in the project. |
| `--none` | Clear the whole pocket again. |
| `-o, --output <OUTPUT>` | Where to write the result; default: the project itself. |

### `chipload op help`

Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

### `chipload op help tool`

Set the tool an operation cuts with (docs/specs/tool-per-operation.md §7). The tool must be in the project: copy one in from your library with `tool use`

```text
chipload op help tool
```

### `chipload op help add-rest`

Add a rest pocket after a pocket (docs/specs/rest-machining.md §10): its shapes and depths, cut with a smaller tool, clearing only what the pocket's tool leaves

```text
chipload op help add-rest
```

### `chipload op help rest`

Make a pocket clear only what a larger tool leaves (docs/specs/rest-machining.md)

```text
chipload op help rest
```

### `chipload op help help`

Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

```text
chipload op help help
```

## `chipload shape`

Draw in a project: add, change or delete circles, rectangles and polylines

### `chipload shape add`

Add a drawn shape; prints its id

```text
chipload shape add <PROJECT> <KIND> [OPTIONS]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<PROJECT>` | The project (.chipload) |
| `<KIND>` | One of: `circle`, `rectangle`, `polyline`. |
| `--center <CENTER>` | Centre "X,Y" (circle, rectangle) |
| `--radius <RADIUS>` |  |
| `--length <LENGTH>` | Along the rectangle's own X axis. |
| `--width <WIDTH>` | Along the rectangle's own Y axis. |
| `--angle-deg <ANGLE_DEG>` | Rotation about the centre, degrees, counter-clockwise. |
| `--points <POINTS>` | Polyline points "X,Y X,Y ...". |
| `--bulges <BULGES>` | Polyline bulges "B B ...", one per segment: tan(sweep / 4) as in DXF, 0 straight, 1 a counter-clockwise half circle, -1 clockwise (default: all straight) |
| `--open` | The polyline doesn't return to its first point. |
| `--closed` | The polyline returns to its first point (the default for new ones) |
| `--layer <LAYER>` |  |
| `-o, --output <OUTPUT>` | Where to write the result; default: the project itself. |

### `chipload shape set`

Change a drawn shape's values or layer; it keeps its id

```text
chipload shape set <PROJECT> <ID> [OPTIONS]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<PROJECT>` | The project (.chipload) |
| `<ID>` | The shape id (as `inspect` lists it, without the S) |
| `--center <CENTER>` | Centre "X,Y" (circle, rectangle) |
| `--radius <RADIUS>` |  |
| `--length <LENGTH>` | Along the rectangle's own X axis. |
| `--width <WIDTH>` | Along the rectangle's own Y axis. |
| `--angle-deg <ANGLE_DEG>` | Rotation about the centre, degrees, counter-clockwise. |
| `--points <POINTS>` | Polyline points "X,Y X,Y ...". |
| `--bulges <BULGES>` | Polyline bulges "B B ...", one per segment: tan(sweep / 4) as in DXF, 0 straight, 1 a counter-clockwise half circle, -1 clockwise (default: all straight) |
| `--open` | The polyline doesn't return to its first point. |
| `--closed` | The polyline returns to its first point (the default for new ones) |
| `--layer <LAYER>` |  |
| `-o, --output <OUTPUT>` | Where to write the result; default: the project itself. |

### `chipload shape delete`

Delete a drawn shape. Operations that used it are flagged

```text
chipload shape delete <PROJECT> <ID> [OPTIONS]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<PROJECT>` | The project (.chipload) |
| `<ID>` |  |
| `-o, --output <OUTPUT>` | Where to write the result; default: the project itself. |

### `chipload shape copy`

Copy drawn shapes, moved by --dx and --dy, on their layers; prints the new ids

```text
chipload shape copy <PROJECT> <IDS>... [OPTIONS]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<PROJECT>` | The project (.chipload) |
| `<IDS>` | The shape ids (as `inspect` lists them, without the S) |
| `--dx <DX>` | How far to move the copies right, mm. Required. |
| `--dy <DY>` | How far to move the copies up, mm. Required. |
| `-o, --output <OUTPUT>` | Where to write the result; default: the project itself. |

### `chipload shape mirror`

Mirror drawn shapes in place, about the middle of the box round them. They keep their ids, so the operations that cut them follow

```text
chipload shape mirror <PROJECT> <IDS>... [OPTIONS]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<PROJECT>` | The project (.chipload) |
| `<IDS>` | The shape ids (as `inspect` lists them, without the S) |
| `--axis <AXIS>` | x: flip the X coordinates (left becomes right); y: flip Y (up becomes down) One of: `x`, `y`. Required. |
| `-o, --output <OUTPUT>` | Where to write the result; default: the project itself. |

### `chipload shape help`

Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

### `chipload shape help add`

Add a drawn shape; prints its id

### `chipload shape help set`

Change a drawn shape's values or layer; it keeps its id

Mirror drawn shapes in place, about the middle of the box round them. They keep their ids, so the operations that cut them follow

## `chipload tool`

Your tool library: tools kept for every project (copied into a project when used)

### `chipload tool export`

Write the tools to a file: a backup, or for another computer

```text
chipload tool export <FILE> [OPTIONS]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<FILE>` |  |
| `--name <NAMES>` | Only these (repeatable); default: all. Repeatable. |

### `chipload tool import`

Add the tools of an exported file (or another computer's library file)

```text
chipload tool import <FILE> [OPTIONS]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<FILE>` |  |
| `--replace` | Overwrite yours where the file has other values under the same name. |

### `chipload tool list`

List the library's tools and where the library is

```text
chipload tool list
```

### `chipload tool add`

Add a tool to the library

```text
chipload tool add <NAME> [OPTIONS]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<NAME>` |  |
| `--type <KIND>` | One of: `endmill`, `drill`, `vbit`. |
| `--diameter <DIAMETER>` |  |
| `--flutes <FLUTES>` |  |
| `--center-cutting <CENTER_CUTTING>` | One of: `yes`, `no`. |
| `--rpm <RPM>` |  |
| `--angle <ANGLE>` | V-bits: the included angle, degrees. |
| `--tip <TIP>` | V-bits: the diameter of the flat tip, mm (0: pointed) |
| `--id <ID>` | The id it gets in a project where that id is free (default 1) |
| `--feed <FEED>` | Cutting values for new operations: give all four the first time. |
| `--plunge-feed <PLUNGE_FEED>` |  |
| `--step-down <STEP_DOWN>` |  |
| `--stepover <STEPOVER>` | Fraction of the tool diameter (pockets) |

### `chipload tool set`

Change a library tool

```text
chipload tool set <NAME> [OPTIONS]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<NAME>` |  |
| `--type <KIND>` | One of: `endmill`, `drill`, `vbit`. |
| `--diameter <DIAMETER>` |  |
| `--flutes <FLUTES>` |  |
| `--center-cutting <CENTER_CUTTING>` | One of: `yes`, `no`. |
| `--rpm <RPM>` |  |
| `--angle <ANGLE>` | V-bits: the included angle, degrees. |
| `--tip <TIP>` | V-bits: the diameter of the flat tip, mm (0: pointed) |
| `--id <ID>` | The id it gets in a project where that id is free (default 1) |
| `--feed <FEED>` | Cutting values for new operations: give all four the first time. |
| `--plunge-feed <PLUNGE_FEED>` |  |
| `--step-down <STEP_DOWN>` |  |
| `--stepover <STEPOVER>` | Fraction of the tool diameter (pockets) |
| `--rename <RENAME>` | A new name. |

### `chipload tool remove`

Remove a tool from the library

```text
chipload tool remove <NAME>
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<NAME>` |  |

### `chipload tool default`

The tool new projects start with

```text
chipload tool default <NAME>
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<NAME>` |  |

### `chipload tool use`

Copy a library tool into a project; prints its id there

```text
chipload tool use <NAME> <PROJECT> [OPTIONS]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<NAME>` |  |
| `<PROJECT>` | The project (.chipload) |
| `-o, --output <OUTPUT>` | Where to write the result; default: the project itself. |

### `chipload tool save`

Save a project's tool into the library

```text
chipload tool save <PROJECT> [OPTIONS]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<PROJECT>` | The project (.chipload) |
| `--tool <TOOL>` | The tool id in the project. Required. |
| `--name <NAME>` | Its name in the library. Required. |
| `--replace` | Overwrite a library tool of that name. |

## `chipload machine`

Your machine profiles: machine values a new project starts with

### `chipload machine export`

Write the machine profiles to a file: a backup, or for another computer

```text
chipload machine export <FILE> [OPTIONS]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<FILE>` |  |
| `--name <NAMES>` | Only these (repeatable); default: all. Repeatable. |

### `chipload machine import`

Add the machine profiles of an exported file (or another computer's library file)

```text
chipload machine import <FILE> [OPTIONS]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<FILE>` |  |
| `--replace` | Overwrite yours where the file has other values under the same name. |

### `chipload machine list`

List the machine profiles and where they are kept

```text

```

### `chipload machine add`

Add a machine profile. Values not given are the built-in project defaults

```text
chipload machine add <NAME> [OPTIONS]
```

|---|---|
| `<NAME>` |  |
| `--post <POST>` | Built-in post-processor. |
| `--safe-z <SAFE_Z>` |  |
| `--spindle <SPINDLE>` | One of: `cw`, `ccw`. |
| `--max-feed <MAX_FEED>` |  |
| `--travel <TRAVEL>` | Travel "X,Y,Z". |
| `--work-zero <WORK_ZERO>` | drawing-origin, stock-center, stock-bottom-left, stock-bottom-right, stock-top-left, stock-top-right, or a point "X,Y". |
| `--max-overcut <MAX_OVERCUT>` | How far below the stock a cut may go (into the spoilboard) |
| `--tool-change <TOOL_CHANGE>` | With several tools: one G-code file per tool, or one file with M6 tool changes that your sender handles. One of: `files` (One G-code file per tool group), `program` (One file with `T<n> M6` at each tool change). |

## `chipload copies`

Cut the part several times in a grid (docs/specs/copies-grid.md)

```text
chipload copies <PROJECT> [OPTIONS]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<PROJECT>` | The project (.chipload) |
| `--grid <GRID>` | Columns x rows, e.g. "3x2". |
| `--pitch <PITCH>` | Pitch "DX,DY" in mm, copy to copy; negative grows left or down. |
| `--gap <GAP>` | Set the pitch so that this many mm are left between the cuts of neighbours. |
| `--order <ORDER>` | The cut order. One of: `by-operation` (Each operation on every copy, then the next operation), `by-part` (Every operation on one copy, then the next copy). |
| `--off` | Back to a single part. |
| `-o, --output <OUTPUT>` | Where to write the result; default: the project itself. |

## `chipload place`

Move, turn or scale the imported drawing (docs/specs/drawing-placement.md, drawing-rotation.md, drawing-scale.md). Without an option, print where it is

```text
chipload place <PROJECT> [OPTIONS]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<PROJECT>` | The project (.chipload) |
| `--by <BY>` | Move by "DX,DY" mm. |
| `--to <TO>` | Put it "DX,DY" mm from where the DXF has it; 0,0 is as drawn. |
| `--align <ALIGN>` | Align the drawing's extent with the stock. One of: `bottom-left` (Bottom-left corner on the stock's, --margin mm in), `center` (Centre on the stock's centre). |
| `--margin <MARGIN>` | With --align bottom-left: how far in from the stock's corner, mm. |
| `--rotate <ROTATE>` | Turn it about its centre, degrees counter-clockwise: 90, 180, 270 or -90. Before --align when both are given. |
| `--scale <SCALE>` | Scale it about its centre by this factor (> 0), on top of any scale it has. After --rotate, before --align. |
| `--width <WIDTH>` | Scale it about its centre until it is this wide, mm (the height follows) |
| `--height <HEIGHT>` | Scale it about its centre until it is this high, mm (the width follows) |
| `--reset` | Back to where the DXF has it: no turn, no scale, no move. |
| `-o, --output <OUTPUT>` | Where to write the result; default: the project itself. |

## `chipload licenses`

Print Chipload's licence and the licences of every third-party component

```text
chipload licenses
```

## `chipload get`

Print a project value by path, as JSON (docs/specs/scripting.md §4), e.g. `operations.1.end_depth`: keys and indexes from 0, as in the file

```text
chipload get <PROJECT> <PATH>
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<PROJECT>` | The project (.chipload) |
| `<PATH>` |  |

## `chipload set`

Set project values by path (docs/specs/scripting.md §4): `operations.1.end_depth=6.5`. A value is JSON when it parses (6.5, true, null, {"after_tool": 1}), else text. The project must still load; problems are listed but don't stop the write

```text
chipload set <PROJECT> <VALUES>... [OPTIONS]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<PROJECT>` | The project (.chipload) |
| `<VALUES>` |  |
| `-o, --output <OUTPUT>` | Where to write the result; default: the project itself. |

## `chipload check-project`

List a project's problems with their paths, without planning; exits 1 if any

```text
chipload check-project <PROJECT>
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<PROJECT>` | The project (.chipload) |

## `chipload schema`

Print the JSON Schema of a file format (docs/specs/scripting.md §2)

```text
chipload schema <FORMAT>
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<FORMAT>` | One of: `project` (A project file (.chipload)), `tools` (The tool library (tools.json, and `tool export` files)), `machines` (The machine profiles (machines.json, and `machine export` files)). |

## `chipload help`

Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

### `chipload help inspect`

Dump units, entities, contours and issues of a DXF or a project

```text
chipload help inspect
```

### `chipload help new`

Create an empty project, to draw in or import a DXF into later (`update --from`)

```text
chipload help new
```

### `chipload help import`

Create a project from a DXF

```text
chipload help import
```

### `chipload help update`

Replace a project's imported drawing with a new version of the DXF

```text
chipload help update
```

### `chipload help plan`

Plan a project's toolpath without writing G-code

```text
chipload help plan
```

### `chipload help run`

Generate checked G-code from a project

```text
chipload help run
```

### `chipload help simulate`

Simulate the material a project's program removes (docs/specs/simulation.md): print the numbers and write a shaded top view (PNG). The job is generated and checked as by `run`; no G-code is written

```text
chipload help simulate
```

### `chipload help sheet`

Write a project's setup sheet for the operator (HTML), without the G-code. The job is generated and checked as by `run`

```text
chipload help sheet
```

### `chipload help render`

Render a toolpath JSON (as `plan --json` prints under "program") through a post-processor. For testing posts; the output is NOT checked, use `run` to cut

```text
chipload help render
```

### `chipload help check`

Check a G-code program against a project's stock, safe height and machine limits

```text
chipload help check
```

### `chipload help op`

Change an operation of a project

Set the tool an operation cuts with (docs/specs/tool-per-operation.md §7). The tool must be in the project: copy one in from your library with `tool use`

### `chipload help op add-rest`

Add a rest pocket after a pocket (docs/specs/rest-machining.md §10): its shapes and depths, cut with a smaller tool, clearing only what the pocket's tool leaves
